title: How Much Experience Should Your Scarsdale Architect Have?
excerpt: When you're planning a renovation or addition in Scarsdale, choosing an architect with the right background matters. Here's what to look for.
content:
If you're thinking about a home renovation or addition in Scarsdale, you've probably started asking yourself what kind of architect you actually need. Experience matters, but it's easy to get confused about what that really means. Some architects have been drawing plans for 30 years. Others have deep roots in your specific community. Some understand both the design side and the construction side. So what should you actually be looking for?

The short answer is this: you want someone who knows how to design your project, understands local building codes and the permit process, and can actually build what they've drawn. That combination is rarer than you might think.

Why Local Knowledge Matters in Scarsdale

Scarsdale has its own building department and its own way of doing things. Every Westchester municipality does. An architect working in Scarsdale needs to understand how your village reviews plans, what they typically ask for, and how long the process usually takes. This isn't about Scarsdale being unusual. It's just that every town has its own rhythm.

When you hire a residential architect in Scarsdale with actual local experience, you're buying something real. They know the inspectors. They know what questions will come up before you even submit paperwork. They've done projects on your street. That saves you time and headaches.

The Power of Having One Person Run Your Project

Here's where a lot of firms drop the ball. They have one architect design your project, then hand it off to a project manager, who coordinates with a general contractor, who talks to the subs. By the time your kitchen remodel or home addition gets built, nobody who drew it is involved anymore.

A design-build architect in Westchester doesn't work that way. When Silvio M. Luca runs your project, he's the licensed architect who designed it and the licensed general contractor who's building it. He shows up. He sees what's happening. He makes decisions on the spot when something needs adjusting. He doesn't disappear after the permit is stamped.

That matters whether you're doing a bathroom renovation or a second-story addition. It matters whether it's historic restoration work or custom new construction. One person responsible means you know who to call and you know they actually care about the outcome.

Look for Real Credentials and Real Presence

When you talk to an architect in Scarsdale, ask whether they're a licensed architect in New York State and whether they're also a licensed general contractor. Ask how many projects they've done in your town. Ask if they'll be overseeing your job personally or if it's being handed off to someone else.

You want someone who has been building homes and renovations across Westchester for years. Someone who understands both the design side and the construction side. Someone who will be there when the walls come down and when the final details get installed.
